title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Ignore the reason for the visit. Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint: Shortness of breath

HPI: The patient is a 68-year-old male presenting for a follow-up regarding chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He reports that his breathing has been manageable over the last month, though he experiences mild exertional dyspnea when walking long distances. He denies any increased productive cough, chest pain, or recent fevers. He reports adherence to his current inhaler regimen and states that his activity level remains consistent.

Medication List: Tiotropium, Salmeterol, Albuterol inhaler as needed.

Exam: The patient is alert and oriented. Respiratory effort is even and unlabored at rest. Lung sounds reveal diminished breath sounds in the lower lobes with bilateral expiratory wheezes. Oxygen saturation is 94% on room air. No peripheral edema noted.

Assessment:
1. COPD: The patient's condition is stable at this time. Symptoms were reviewed and are currently well-controlled.

Plan:
1. COPD: Continue current medications as prescribed. The plan is to monitor for any increased respiratory distress. Follow up in three months.
explanations: The provider addressed COPD at this visit (status and plan documented), so it is supported and coded.

distractors.why: Status plus a plan in the assessment supports the diagnosis.

hccs.label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease/Interstitial Lung Disorders/and Other Chronic Lung Disorders
